questions.q: If $2  \left(y - a\right)$ is the harmonic mean between $y - x$ and $y - z$, then $x - a, y - a$ and $z - a are in$
questions.solution:
It is given that, $y - x, 2 \left(y - a\right)and \left(y - z\right)$ are in harmonic progression.

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{y - x}, \dfrac{1}{2\left(y - a\right)}, \dfrac{1}{y - z}$are in arithmetic progression.

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{2\left(y - a\right)} - \dfrac{1}{y - x} = \dfrac{1}{y - z} - \dfrac{1}{2\left(y - a\right)}$

$⇒\dfrac{2a - y - x}{y - x} = \dfrac{y + z - 2a}{y - z}$

$⇒ \dfrac{\left(x - a\right) + \left(y - a\right)}{\left(x - a\right) - \left(y - a\right)} = \dfrac{\left(y - a\right) + \left(z - a\right)}{\left(y - a\right) - \left(z - a\right)}$

$⇒\dfrac{x - a}{y - a} = \dfrac{y - a}{z - a}$

Hence, $x - a, y - aandz - a$ are in geometric progression

questions.solution:
Let $A$ be the 1^{st}term and $ R$ be the common ratio of the given G.P.

Sum of the first $n$ terms of the G.P. is $x = \dfrac{A ( 1 - R^{n} )}{1 - R}$. The next $n$ terms form a G.P. series of $n$ terms with the first term as the ${\left(n + 1\right)}^{th}$ term of the given G.P. is given by ${t}_{n + 1} = AR^{n}$. Sum of the next $n$ terms of the G.P. is $y ⇒ y = \dfrac{AR^{n} ( 1 - R^{n} )}{1 - R}$ and

$z = AR^{2n}\dfrac{\left(1 - R^{n}\right)}{1 - R}⇒ y^{2} = zx$

$∴x$, $y$, $z$ are in G.P.

questions.solution:
The roots of $10{x}^{3} - c{x}^{2} - 54x - 27 = 0$ are in H.P.
Replacing $x$ by $\dfrac{1}{x}$ we will get an equation whose roots will be in A.P.
$⇒ \dfrac{10}{{x}^{3}} - \dfrac{c}{{x}^{2}} - \dfrac{54}{x} - 27 = 0 ⇒ 27{x}^{3} + 54{x}^{2} + cx - 10 = 0$
Hence, roots of this equation are in A.P. i.e. $a - d, a, a + d$
$\left(a - d\right) + a + \left(a + d\right) = - \dfrac{54}{27} = - 2 ⇒ a = - \dfrac{2}{3}$
Since $a$ is the root of the given equation
$⇒ 27{\left(- \dfrac{2}{3}\right)}^{3} + 54{\left(- \dfrac{2}{3}\right)}^{2} + c\left(- \dfrac{2}{3}\right) - 10 = 0$
$⇒ - 8 + 24 - 10 = \dfrac{2c}{3} ⇒ c = \dfrac{6 \times 3}{2} = 9$
$c = 9$

so, ${\left(a - b\right)}^{2} = {\left(a + b\right)}^{2} - 4ab = {\left(\dfrac{75}{2}\right)}^{2} - 4 \times 225$
$= \left(\dfrac{75}{2} + 30\right)\left(\dfrac{75}{2} - 30\right) = \dfrac{135}{2} \times \dfrac{15}{2}$
$⇒ a - b = \pm \left(\dfrac{15}{2} \times$3\right) = $\pm \left(\dfrac{45}{2}\right)

$⇒ a = 30, b = \dfrac{45}{2}$
Case2 $\to a + b = \dfrac{75}{2}, a - b = - \dfrac{45}{2}$
$⇒ a = \dfrac{15}{2}, b = 30$
So, larger of the two numbers is 30

questions.q: Let $a, b, c$ and $d$ are in a geometric progression such that $a < b < c < d, a + d = 112$ and $b + c = 48.$ If the geometric progression is continued with $a$ as the first term, then the sum of the first six terms is
questions.solution:
Let $r$ be the common ratio
$a + d = 112 ⇒ a + ar^{3} = 112$
$b + c = 48 ⇒ ar + ar^{2} = 48$
Dividing the first equation by the second equation we get
$\dfrac{a\left(1 + r^{3}\right)}{a\left(1 + r\right)r} = \dfrac{112}{48} = \dfrac{\left(1 + r\right)\left(1 - r + r^{2}\right)}{r\left(r + 1\right)} = \dfrac{7}{3}$
$⇒ 3r^{2} - 3r + 3 = 7r$
$⇒ 3r^{2} - 10r + 3 = 0$
$r = 3$ or $\dfrac{1}{3}$
Given they are in ascending order $⇒ r = 3$
$r = 3 ⇒ a = \dfrac{112}{1 + r^{3}} = \dfrac{112}{28} = 4$
$⇒ a = 4, b = 12, c = 36, d = 108$
$⇒$ Sum of first $6$ terms $= \dfrac{4 ( {3}^{6} - 1 )}{( 3 - 1 )} = 1456$

Replace $n$ by $\left(n - 1\right)$
$\left({1}^{2} + {2}^{2} + {3}^{3} + . \ldots \ldots + {\left(n - 1\right)}^{2}\right) - \left({a}_{1} + {a}_{2} + {a}_{3} + . \ldots \ldots + {a}_{n - 1}\right) = \dfrac{1}{3}\left(n - 1\right)\left({\left(n - 1\right)}^{2} - 1\right)$

questions.solution:
For the A.P. let $a$ be the first term and $d$ be the common difference

Given ${T}_{p + 1} = 2{T}_{q + 1}$
$⇒ a + pd = 2\left(a + qd\right) ⇒ a = \left(p - 2q\right)d$
Also,
${T}_{3p + 1} = \lambda{T}_{p + q + 1}$
$a + 3pd = \lambda\left(a + \left(p + q\right)d\right)$
$a\left(\lambda - 1\right) = d\left(3p - \lambdap - \lambdaq\right)
So, \left(p - 2q\right)d = \dfrac{\left(\lambdap + \lambdaq - 3p\right)d}{1 - \lambda}$
$⇒ p - p\lambda - 2q + 2q\lambda = \lambdap + \lambdaq - 3p$
$⇒ \lambda \left(p + q + p - 2q\right) = p - 2q + 3p$
$⇒ \lambda = \dfrac{4p - 2q}{2p - q} = \dfrac{2 \left(2p - q\right)}{2p - q} = 2$
